description:
FOUND s493 (Fable, 2026-09-20) by the ONE-LINER battery (pkrumins' perl1line.txt, 177 one-liners = the canonical list of what people type at a shell).  `pcl --help`: -e -E -I -M -c -w -v only.
MEASURED: the SEMANTICS are already there.  ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s493/angles/oneliners/run1l.pl expands each switch into perlrun's documented source form (-n => `LINE: while (<>) { ... }`, -p => + `continue { print or die }`, -l => `$\ = $/` + chomp, -a/-F => `our @F = split(...)`, -i => `$^I`, -0 => `$/`), has PERL validate the expansion against the real one-liner, then runs the expanded script under pcl: **141 of 152 valid one-liners are byte-identical to perl** (`<>`, `$.`, `eof`, flip-flop `1..10`, END blocks, `$^I` in-place edit all work).  The 11 misses: #2090 (`()=<>`), MIME::Base64 x4 (XS, shim planned), smartmatch x2 (ruled), bignum `bpi(n)` x2, List::Util `max` on non-numeric strings (returns the first of equals, perl the last).
SIZE: a driver-level SOURCE EXPANSION in `pcl` (the table above is ~40 lines of perl; cluster parsing like -lane / -i.bak / -0777 / -F: included), plus the `#!perl -w`-line switches of a SCRIPT FILE (perl honours -n/-p/-l/-a/-i/-0 on the shebang line too).  No compiler or runtime change.  Guard: tools/t or Pl/t rows driving `pcl` with each switch; the battery itself (run1l.pl with the expansion turned OFF) becomes the acceptance test.


=== USER RULING s494 (2026-09-21) ===
Asked with the other three s493 proposals (AskUserQuestion): NOT selected for scheduling; the USER then said: "Please put the other alternatives to the last question on the todo, but not so prioritized."  So this task is ON THE TODO, LOW PRIORITY: it is a wanted feature (no longer an open USER decision), it takes a slot only when nothing scheduled is waiting (after #2104, #2098, #2106), and it is never a reason to delay a correctness or perf round.  The measurement stands: the SEMANTICS exist (141 of 152 expanded one-liners identical); the work is the switch parsing in `pcl` + perlrun`s documented source expansion, with perl1line.txt as the acceptance corpus.

=== DONE (s506f, Opus, 2026-10-04; resumed s507, final bars on 3756b678 = main d23b5927 + the batch, branch worktree-agent-a908d9d2d9fff4ce2) ===
perl's command-line switches in `pcl`: ONE parser (tools/lib/PCLSwitches.pm parse_argv: clusters, `--`, `-`, stdin program, perl's switch errors, status 25) and ONE expansion in pl2cl (`--switches=HEX` merged with the program's own #! line, perlrun's equivalents on the first code line, no line moves).  Table: docs/pcl-commands.md; what differs: docs/not-supported.md "Perl's command-line switches".  -n -p -a -F -l -0 -g -i -s -x -S -E -I -M -m -c -w -C implemented; -T/-t run + announced; -W -X -U -f inert; -D perl's message; -d -u refused; -v = version, -V/-V:name from %Config, -h/-?; a script's #! line honoured (#1702).  Guards: Pl/t/pcl-switches-01.t (122 rows), tools/t/harness-switches.t rows 5-11, Pl/t/script-cache-01.t (+5).  One-liner battery 147 of 152 (ol-052 #2665, ol-062/064 #2664, ol-161/164 smartmatch).  Companion: run/switches.t 29/111 -> 125/15, switchC 3/12 -> 12/3, switchx 0/2 -> 7/1, switch0 OK, switchI 0/4 -> 2/2, re/recompile.t 0/48 -> 24/24.  Sweep TOTAL 18728 -> 18731.  EVERYDAY 113 -> 113.  Residue: #2660-#2670 (#1709's switch residue = #2667).
subject: FEATURE (USER s494: on the todo, LOW priority): the `pcl` command has none of perl's one-liner switches -- -n -p -l -a -F -i -0 (-s) are missing, so `pcl -pe 's/foo/bar/'`, `pcl -lane 'print $F[0]'`, `pcl -i.bak -pe ...` cannot be written at all
